summary: Deployed a MariaDB Galera cluster on node1-node3 (bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster), created an appdb.orders table with an appuser account (password generated on-node via /dev/urandom), and verified multi-master writes replicate across all three. Added node4 by updating its galera.cnf (wsrep_cluster_address including all four hosts) and starting mariadb, which triggered an automatic SST (rsync) that fully copied the existing data; confirmed node4 can accept writes that replicate back to the original members. Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes (SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered them). Then ran the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on each of the 4 nodes one at a time: captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and Galera health baseline, issued a delayed `systemctl reboot` so the ack returned first, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the node rejoined the cluster (wsrep_cluster_size=4, state Synced, status Primary) with all appdb.orders rows intact before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, galera on node1-4 via dnf
Configured /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all 4 nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567/4568 (tcp+udp where applicable) on all 4 nodes
Edited /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-3 (wsrep_on=1, cluster_name, cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, node_name, node_address)
Bootstrapped 3-node Galera cluster via galera_new_cluster on node1
Started mariadb on node2 and node3, confirmed join to wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced
Enabled mariadb service on boot for node1-3
Created appdb.orders table, seeded rows, created appuser with on-node-generated random password, verified replication to node2/node3
Inserted a row from node2 and confirmed it appeared on node1 (multi-master write proof)
Configured node4 galera.cnf with cluster_address including node4, updated node1-3 configs' cluster_address for future restarts
Started mariadb on node4; it joined via automatic SST (rsync), receiving full existing dataset
Verified wsrep_cluster_size=4, Synced, appdb.orders present, appuser present on node4
Inserted a row from node4 and confirmed it replicated to node3
Enabled mariadb on boot for node4

Ran restart-evidence protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3, node4: captured boot_id + Galera health baseline, background-delayed systemctl reboot, polled boot_id until changed, verified mariadb active and cluster rejoined (size=4, Synced, Primary) with data intact before proceeding to next node
